# SHOT LIST — "Made by the hands that use it" (handmade ceramic mug)

**Format:** 9:16 vertical · 15 s · target model: Kling (text-to-video, silent; sound added in edit)
**Input:** *"15s vertical ad for a handmade ceramic mug, for Kling. just go."* (all intake defaults used)
**Logline:** A potter's fingertips shape a spinning rim of wet clay, and the finished mug ends up in those same hands for the first sip of the morning.

> Using the real product? This plan is text-to-video, so Kling will invent *a* mug, not
> *your* mug. For a real listing, photograph the actual mug once and run S2, S3 and S5 as
> image-to-video from that photo (prompt = motion + camera only, see "I2V variants" below).

## Crew notes

**Director**
- INTENT: "handmade" should be something you *see* (clay on fingers, uneven rim, thumb dimple), not something you're told. Viewer wants to hold it.
- HOOK (0–1.5 s): overhead macro of fingertips smoothing a spinning wet clay rim. Motion from frame 1, readable with sound off.
- BEATS: 1) clay rim shaped by hand · 2) finished mug, steaming (product on screen by 2.5 s) · 3) thumb settles into the handle dimple · 4) potter sips · 5) mug set down, seen from above
- ENDING: overhead circle of the mug rim → match cut back to the overhead circle of the clay rim in S1 (loop).

**Production designer — continuity bible** (paste verbatim; never paraphrase)
- C1 `a woman in her 40s, grey-streaked brown hair tied back, light olive skin, freckles, wearing a clay-streaked rust-orange canvas apron over a cream linen shirt, a thin silver ring on the right index finger`
- C1-H (C1's hands, for hands-only shots) `clay-dusted hands with short bare nails and a thin silver ring on the right index finger`
- P1 `a handmade stoneware mug with a matte speckled oatmeal-white glaze that stops short of the bare brown clay foot, a slightly uneven rim, and a thick loop handle with a thumb dimple on top`
  - state S2–S4: `filled with black coffee` · state S5: `two-thirds full of black coffee`
- P2 `a wet grey-brown clay cylinder spinning on a pottery wheel, glistening with slip` (slip = watery liquid clay)
- L1 `a small pottery studio with a whitewashed brick wall, wooden shelves of unglazed bowls, and a worn pine worktable`
- L1-T (tight-shot version of L1) `on a worn pine worktable, a whitewashed brick wall far out of focus behind`
- PALETTE: oatmeal white, rust orange, warm clay brown, slate grey
- No maker's stamp, logo or lettering on the mug (would render as gibberish). Brand goes on the end card in the edit.

**DP / Gaffer**
- Tight and mostly locked-off (tripod, no movement): macro on the two hand shots, one slow push-in on the product hero and one on the face. Sizes alternate ECU → CU → ECU → MCU → CU so no cut looks like a jump.
- One source for the whole piece: soft late-morning window light from camera-left, warm highlights against cool blue-grey shadows (~4500K key vs ~6500K ambient), medium contrast, a thin backlight edge on the glaze to separate the mug. Look: 35mm film, Kodak Portra 400, fine grain.

**Editor**
- 96 BPM track, cuts land on the bar: S1 2.5 s · S2 2.5 s · S3 2.5 s · S4 3.75 s · S5 3.75 s = **15.0 s**.
- Generate every shot at **5 s** in Kling (its shortest standard length), use the cleanest middle section. That's 1.25–2.5 s of handles (spare frames to trim) per shot.
- Cuts: S1→S2 hard cut (raw clay → finished mug) · S2→S3 cut on the push-in, into the handle · S3→S4 cut on action (grip → sip) · S4→S5 cut on the downward motion · S5→S1 match cut, circle to circle, for the loop.
- Text (in edit, upper third, clear of the bottom 15%): 0.3–2.5 s "Thrown by hand." · 11.6–15.0 s end card "<brand> · handmade stoneware · link in bio".

**Sound** (added in edit; Kling prompts stay silent)
- MUSIC: warm acoustic guitar, 96 BPM, gentle build to S4.
- SFX: S1 wheel hum + wet clay hiss · S3 soft ceramic tap of a ring on the handle · S4 quiet sip · S5 ceramic clunk on wood.

**Script supervisor**
- ✅ "Handmade" was a mood → translated into visible proof: clay on fingers (S1), uneven rim + bare clay foot (S2), thumb dimple (S3).
- ✅ S4 first draft was "lifts the mug and sips" (two actions) → now starts with the mug already at her lips.
- ✅ S3 first draft had a slow truck (sideways camera move) *and* a hand grip → camera locked off; the hand is the only motion.
- ✅ Full L1 descriptor in the macro shots pulled shelves and bowls into frame on paper → macro shots use the locked L1-T variant instead.
- ✅ Maker's stamp on the mug removed (text).
- ✅ Screen direction: hands enter from camera-right in S3 and S5; key light stays camera-left everywhere.
- ✅ Prop state: full in S2–S4, two-thirds in S5 (after the sip).
- ⚠️ HIGHEST RISK: S1 (hands + deformable spinning clay). Kept overhead, macro, locked, fingertips only, no other objects.

## Shots

| # | Time | Size · Lens · Move | Action (one) | Gen | Risk |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | 0.0–2.5 | ECU · 100mm macro · locked-off, overhead | fingertips smooth the rim of the spinning clay | 5 s | **high** |
| S2 | 2.5–5.0 | CU · 85mm · slow push-in, eye level | steam rises from the coffee in P1 | 5 s | low |
| S3 | 5.0–7.5 | ECU · 100mm macro · locked-off, side angle | hand grips the handle, thumb settles into the dimple | 5 s | med |
| S4 | 7.5–11.25 | MCU · 50mm · slow push-in, eye level | C1 takes a slow sip, mug held at her lips | 5 s | med |
| S5 | 11.25–15.0 | CU · 50mm · locked-off, overhead | hand sets P1 down and lets go; coffee ripples, settles | 5 s | med |

(ECU = extreme close-up; CU = close-up; MCU = chest-up.)

## Prompts

Kling order: subject → movement → scene → camera → lighting → atmosphere.

### S1
```
A wet grey-brown clay cylinder spinning on a pottery wheel, glistening with slip, and clay-dusted hands with short bare nails and a thin silver ring on the right index finger. Two fingertips press lightly on the clay rim, smoothing it as it spins at real-time speed. On a worn pine worktable, a whitewashed brick wall far out of focus behind. Overhead top-down extreme close-up, 100mm macro lens, locked-off camera. Soft window light from camera-left, cool blue-grey shadows, wet highlights on the clay. 35mm film, Kodak Portra 400, fine grain.
```
Negative: `extra fingers, fused fingers, warped hands, melting clay, morphing, collapsing pot, flicker, text, logo, watermark, oversaturated`

### I2V variants (if you have a real photo of the mug)
Use the photo as the first frame. Prompt motion + camera only:
- S2: `A thin wisp of steam rises and curls from the coffee. Slow push-in, 85mm. Real-time speed.`
- S3: `A clay-dusted hand with a thin silver ring on the right index finger enters from camera-right and grips the handle; the thumb settles into the dimple. Locked-off camera.`
- S5: `The coffee surface ripples gently, then settles. Locked-off overhead camera.` (drop the hand; set-down is hard to fake from a still)

## Reroll plan

| Shot | Likely failure | Change before reroll |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | fingers merge into the clay, or the pot collapses/morphs | Remove the hands entirely: "the clay rim spins, a thin ridge of slip rising" (still reads handmade). If hands are a must, I2V from a real photo of fingertips on the wheel. |
| S2 | mug looks glossy/plastic and perfectly symmetrical | Move "slightly uneven rim, matte speckled glaze" to the very start of the prompt; keep everything else fixed. |
| S3 | extra/fused fingers, or a second handle appears | Cut the entry: start with the hand already on the handle, only the thumb moves into the dimple. |
| S4 | mug merges into face, or she drinks twice / lowers it | Reframe to a profile (side view) MCU so the mug and mouth don't overlap on the lens axis. |
| S5 | mug tips or slides, coffee sloshes over the rim | Drop the hand: generate the mug already on the table, coffee ripples settling only. |

**Highest-risk shot:** S1 — deformable spinning clay plus fingertips is two hard-physics problems in one frame, and it's the hook, so it can't be weak. Have the hands-free fallback ready before you spend a third generation on it.
